implementation_notes: The screen state is an immutable data class held in a MutableStateFlow behind a read-only StateFlow; commands are methods that call update {}, and the view collects the flow (collectAsStateWithLifecycle in Compose, repeatOnLifecycle elsewhere). A StateFlow is hot and always in memory and replays the current state to every new collector, so no extra replay logic is needed; viewModelScope ties background work to the state holder and the ViewModel documentation names it the place for UI-layer logic that outlives the view.
pitfalls: StateFlow conflates by equality: emitting an equal state does not notify collectors, so a state class without a discriminating field swallows updates.

Collecting a StateFlow never stops by itself - the Android documentation contrasts this with LiveData, which unregisters at STOPPED - so collection must be lifecycle-aware (repeatOnLifecycle, collectAsStateWithLifecycle).
A ViewModel must not hold Context, View or other lifecycle-related references, and viewModelScope work must be cancelled-aware: the documentation warns that these leak or outlive the owner.

variants.name: Compose state holder using mutableStateOf inside a plain class
variants.idiom_name: plain holder with mutableStateOf fields + remember/rememberSaveable
variants.implementation_notes: In Compose the UI is a function of state, so the presentation model is a plain class holding MutableState fields (or a StateFlow converted with collectAsStateWithLifecycle): the composable reads the state and re-renders on change, while the holder owns the commands. remember keeps the holder across recompositions and rememberSaveable across configuration changes; the Compose runtime performs the observation, so no binding code is written at all, and the holder itself is still an ordinary testable object.
pitfalls: mutableStateOf uses structural equality by default, so writing an equal value does not recompose; use a non-equality policy where every write must notify.
State created with remember is lost on process death - rememberSaveable (or a ViewModel with SavedStateHandle) is required for state that must survive it.
Reading state outside composition (in a coroutine or callback) does not create a dependency unless it is wrapped in snapshotFlow or read inside a composable.
